chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) about a Jew or a Christian who divorced his wife with one divorce, then both he and his wife embraced Islam; what is their status? He said:

"He marries her with a new marriage contract." I asked, "If he divorces her after his Islam with one or two divorces, does she observe the waiting period based on the divorce that occurred before her Islam?" He said, "She does not observe the waiting period based on that."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a non-Muslim couple who convert to Islam after the husband has already divorced his wife once?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the pre-Islamic divorce is nullified upon the couple's conversion, necessitating a fresh marriage contract (nikah jadid) to re-establish the marital bond. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the validity of divorce is contingent upon the Islamic status of the parties, meaning the wife does not observe an iddah based on the prior pagan divorce but rather on the new Islamic union.
